newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian share correction seen extending lower.
newsitem.headline: Russian share correction seen extending lower.

text.p: Leading Russian shares fell early on Tuesday as some Western investors took profits after a month-long runup. Traders said the correction could last several days and knock 10 percent off the market's peak value.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened slightly off its Monday close at 503.40 from 504.55. The record set late Monday was 507.75.

National electricity company UES EESR.RTS dropped to $0.4450 at 0840 GMT from $0.4610 at the previous close and oil producer LUKoil LKOH.RTS fell to $22.00 from $22.65, though up from a morning low of around $21.67.

"Westerners are taking profits, at the margins some Russians buying," said Brunswick director Martin Diggle who saw the correction lasting a few days and the market easing up to 10 percent from highs set in the last couple of days.

Trading volume declined, typical of a falling Russian market. Mosenergo MSNG.RTS, down from a Monday high of $1.70, had traded about $3.4 million by 0825 GMT. Shares were last trading at $1.566 from just under $1.60 late on Monday.

"Not a huge volume considering the price move," said Rinaco-Plus trader Tom Brackenbury, referring to early Mosenergo turnover. "We do not see major foreign selling -- there is just no major buying from overseas," he added.

Diggle said well over $1 billion had been poured into the market, chiefly a dozen leading shares, over the last month, as the RTS index rose from the 360s level. Traders said investors had more cash earmarked for Russia.
"It is a correction, not a bear market," Brackenbury said. "There still is a lot of money with the Russia label stuck on it that hasn't been allocated even now."
